title: OpenAI says AI models improved AMD’s upcoming GPU design by up to 14% on PPA
summary: OpenAI models improve AMD upcoming GPU design by up to 14 percent
detailed: OpenAI announced that its undisclosed AI models optimized AMD's upcoming flagship GPU and CPU designs, achieving up to a 14% Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) improvement in GPU circuitry.
The optimization condensed an estimated year of conventional chip-design work into under 5 months by rewriting SystemVerilog RTL code.
Involved companies include OpenAI, AMD, and Synopsys.
This matters because it highlights the capability of high-end LLMs to function as expert microarchitects, significantly accelerating semiconductor design and optimization.
sentences: OpenAI says AI models helped optimize AMD’s upcoming flagship GPU and CPU designs, with up to 14% PPA improvement in the GPU circuitry and unspecified single-digit gains for the processor.
OpenAI has shared new details about its ongoing partnership with AMD.
Engineers used undisclosed AI models to optimize designs for AMD’s upcoming flagship GPU and CPUs.

OpenAI said its model identified “further improvements by rewriting the code that describes the chip’s circuits.” The work was done in SystemVerilog RTL, a language commonly used for high-end chip design.
The company said the optimization was equivalent to condensing a year of conventional chip-design work into “under 5 months,” a pace it described as unprecedented in the field.

OpenAI said the model reasoned about RTL “at the level of an expert microarchitect.” The company expects to achieve further PPA improvements in both GPU and CPU designs beyond the current improved baseline.
OpenAI also described tests of its high-end LLMs, which were asked to optimize the PicoRV32 and Ibex chip cores.
Each model run received 112,000 tokens and was scored on throughput, combining Instructions-per-Clock with clock-cycle duration.
A design scored zero if it did not work or used more than 16x the area of the previous design; the best designs meeting the test constraints received 1.0.
The models were not told which workloads the chips would run.
OpenAI said GPT-6.2 Astra performed best on both measures, achieving the lowest overall cost and the highest optimization score.
A second test found that the models produced better results when redesigning chips from their initial specifications than when optimizing existing code.
OpenAI did not say whether researchers used unmodified versions of GPT.
The company said it is working with Synopsys to train GPT-Synopsis, a model for using chip-design tools.
OpenAI has also worked with Broadcom on Jalapeño, an inference-focused chip.
Engineering samples were running actual workloads as early as June 2026.
The company expected small initial deployments around late 2026 and a broader rollout in 2027.
Published test benchmarks have claimed power and latency savings compared with Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in single-token prediction workloads.
